title: Andy Cooks' Hyderabadi Chicken Dum Biryani
ingredients: 2 lbs bone-in or boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces
2 cups aged long-grain Basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 mins
3 large yellow/red onions, thinly sliced and fried golden crisp (birista)
2 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp garam masala, 2 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp cumin
2 green chilies (slit), 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves, 1/2 cup fresh cilantro, juice of 1 lemon
Whole spices for rice: 4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp shahi jeera (caraway/cumin)
Pinch of saffron threads steeped in 1/4 cup warm milk + 2 tbsp ghee
instructions: Fry the thinly sliced onions in oil over medium heat for 15–20 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy (birista); drain on paper towels.

Marinate the chicken in the bottom of a heavy Dutch oven with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili, turmeric, garam masala, coriander, cumin, lemon juice, salt, half the crispy fried onions, and half the chopped mint and cilantro for at least 1 hour.
Boil a large pot of well-salted water with the whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves, cumin). Boil the soaked Basmati rice for 5–6 minutes until 70% cooked; drain immediately.
Layer the 70%-cooked Basmati rice directly over the raw marinated chicken (kacchi dum style). Top with the remaining crispy onions, mint, cilantro, saffron milk, and melted ghee.

Seal the Dutch oven tightly with foil and a heavy lid. Cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until steam builds, then turn heat to the lowest setting (or bake at 325°F) for 35–40 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before gently fluffing from the bottom.
